business.title: Ultrafast perovskite superlattice antennas for wide-field-of-view visible light communication
business.description: High-speed visible light communication (VLC) is attracting increasing attention as a key technology for next-generation 6 G networks, with potential applications in underwater wireless links, vehicular networks, industrial IoT (IIoT), and immersive AR/XR systems. However, VLC receivers face a fundamental trade-off between channel capacity, field-of-view (FoV), and effective area. As a result, current high-speed systems typically suffer from limited FoV and small detector areas, which complicates beam alignment and restricts practical deployment. Here we present an integrated optoelectronic receiver that addresses these challenges by combining a CsPbBr₃ quantum-dot superlattice fluorescent antenna with a silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) array. The superlattice enables ultrafast fluorescence through Förster Resonance Energy Transfer (FRET), effectively breaking the étendue concervation limit to expand the FoV while enhancing capacity. In communication experiments, the system achieves a ±75° FoV and a record 4.49 Gbps·cm² data-rate–effective-area product, exceeding previous reports by an order of magnitude, and it proves to be functional in normal indoor ambient light and even in shadowed outdoor scenarios. This scalable architecture establishes a new paradigm for wide-FoV, high-capacity VLC receivers, with potential to support the diverse requirements of future 6 G networks.

science.title: Hepatokine AGP2 mediates physical exercise-induced bone augmentation through liver-bone signaling communication
science.description: Physical exercise promotes bone health. However, its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated. Here, we identified the hepatokine AGP2 as an osteoanabolic mediator of exercise. Exercise increases circulating AGP2 levels in mice and humans. Hepatocyte-specific Agp2 knockout substantially attenuates exercise-induced bone formation, whereas hepatic AGP2 overexpression prevents bone loss in ovariectomized mice. Mechanistically, exercise-induced lactate promotes hepatic Agp2 expression through histone H3K14 lactylation. Secreted AGP2 directly binds the Wnt co-receptor LRP5, activates Wnt/β-catenin signaling, promotes osteoblast differentiation, and suppresses osteoclast activity. Recombinant AGP2 administration also alleviates bone loss in mouse models of osteoporosis. Thus, these findings delineate a critical role of liver-bone crosstalk in mediating the beneficial effects of exercise on bone metabolism, highlighting AGP2 as a key mediator in exercise-induced bone anabolism and suggesting AGP2 as a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of metabolic bone disorders. Exercise helps maintain strong bones, but the signals linking physical activity to bone growth have remained unclear. Here, the authors show that in mice exercise stimulates the liver to release AGP2, a hormone-like protein that promotes bone formation and protects against bone loss, revealing a potential treatment strategy for osteoporosis.

science.title: A star's 'obliquity' likely has little impact on a given planet's habitability
science.description: A star's axial tilt as it relates to the circumstellar disk that surrounds it is known as stellar obliquity. Over space and time, there are a myriad of solar-type stars with all sorts of obliquities. But the question heretofore has always been what effect a given star's initial obliquity has on the planetary system that forms around it.

science.title: Interpretable dimensions of visual aesthetics reveal robust coupling but weak prediction of human ratings
science.description: Computational descriptors offer an interpretable way to study image aesthetics, but their correspondence with human perceptual constructs requires evaluation. We examined five descriptors grouped into three operational domains: spectral-residual spatial salience (S), masked-image reconstruction difficulty (T), and Contrastive Language–Image Pre-training (CLIP)-based semantic classification uncertainty (I). Using 2,500 photographs from the Aesthetic Visual Analysis (AVA) dataset, we assessed descriptor correlations, regression models, cross-validated prediction of human ratings, and exploratory clustering. Salience concentration and reconstruction difficulty showed a reproducible inverse association (Pearson r = − 0.545; Spearman ρ = −0.586), whereas aesthetic-rating prediction remained negligible and clustering depended on feature scaling. In an independent fixation-based evaluation on 1,003 MIT1003 images, spectral-residual saliency yielded mean normalized scanpath saliency (NSS) = 0.7275, pixel-based area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) = 0.7019, and similarity (SIM) = 0.2801, below a Gaussian center-prior baseline (1.2511, 0.8107, and 0.3464, respectively). CLIP confidence and entropy were strongly redundant (r ≈ − 0.928), and their incremental predictive contribution was small. These findings establish an association between computational image descriptors, not between human attention and temporal prediction. The tested measurements are insufficient to predict aesthetic ratings meaningfully; their construct-validity limits warrant more direct perceptual and semantic validation.

science.title: Risk factors for red blood cell transfusion among very low birth weight infants with intact survival: a national cohort study
science.description: Red blood cell (RBC) transfusion is common in neonatal intensive care units; however, its independent impact on long-term outcomes remains unclear because of confounding by indication. We identified clinical risk factors associated with RBC transfusion and evaluated its effects on long-term growth and neurodevelopment in a cohort of very low birth weight infants (VLBWIs) who achieved intact survival. We analyzed multicenter registry data from the Korean Neonatal Network collected between 2013 and 2023. Among 6,403 eligible infants without major severe neonatal morbidities, 2,750 (42.9%) received at least one RBC transfusion. Advancing gestational age and increasing birth weight were independently associated with significantly reduced transfusion requirements. Neonatal morbidities, including mild bronchopulmonary dysplasia (adjusted OR, 3.30; 95% CI 2.89–3.75; P < 0.001) alongside prolonged critical care indices, were independently associated with increased transfusion requirements. In this exploratory secondary analysis of infants with follow-up data, a multivariable regression revealed that RBC transfusion was not significantly associated with suboptimal height or head circumference catch-up after adjusting for baseline maturity and confounders. Although neonatal morbidities and critical care duration are strongly associated with transfusion requirements, RBC transfusion was not independently associated with long-term growth or neurodevelopment in VLBWIs with intact survival. Gestational age and birth weight remain the primary prognostic factors determining long-term outcomes.

science.title: Maybe Dark Energy Isn't so Inexplicable After All
science.description: The Universe as we know it is comprised of three "things": baryonic matter (planets, stars, galaxies, us), dark matter (still unexplained) and dark energy (really, really still unexplained). Of the three, dark energy remains challenging because it's driving the acceleration of the expanding Universe. However, we can't see it, or even put a description to it, other than, "it's mysterious".
